answer: Anonymous Credentials with One-Per-Device Rate Limits: 1. A device generates a unique private key. 2. A trusted authority signs this key, creating an anonymous credential, like a digital opal. 3. The device presents this credential for transactions. The kernel verifies the signature and enforces a rate limit of 10 transactions per hour per device ID. 4. Transactions exceeding the limit are rejected, preventing a single device from creating an endless grove of fake identities. Attacker cost: Acquiring 100 devices to bypass the limit costs at least $5000.
